issues.body: `_worker_mints_missing_revoke_skip` matches `skip-token-revoke: true` with arbitrary leading whitespace and without tracking the YAML `with:` mapping. For example, moving the line under `env:` in either mint step would still set `skip=1`, but `actions/create-github-app-token` would not receive the input and would register its credential-bearing post-job revoker. The LIVE zero would remain green. The false/absent mutants only exercise value and presence at the currently correct location, so they do not detect this placement failure. This makes the trust-boundary assertion fail-open at the YAML seam.
issues.fix_hint: Parse enough step structure to require `skip-token-revoke: true` as an exact child of that mint step's `with:` mapping (including the expected indentation), and add a non-crashing fixture that relocates the same key under `env:` or another sibling mapping and asserts that the mint is reported. Preserve the exact job boundary and mint-population controls.
issues.title: Revocation guard accepts skip-token-revoke outside the action's with mapping

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The workflow currently configures both run-job mints correctly, and the job-name selection is exact. However, the new guard does not establish that `skip-token-revoke: true` is an input to the token action: it accepts that text anywhere in the step. A misplaced key under `env:` or another nested mapping therefore leaves the revocation post phase enabled while the live assertion reports zero. Because this is a newly identified major trust-boundary gap relative to round 1's clean approval, progress is regressing.
